For Respondent(s) : Mr. Sriram Choudhary, PP  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE MUKESH RAJPUROHIT Order 07/08/2025 1.
After arguing for some time, learned counsel for the petitioner does not want to press the instant criminal misc. [2025:RJ-JD:35095] (2 of 3) [CRLMP-6354/2025] petition.

However, he seeks liberty for the petitioner to submit a representation to the concerned Superintendent of Police with Smt. Geeta Devi Chandak vs State Of Rajasthan (2025:Rj-Jd:35095) on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125591048/
1 appropriate directions to decide the same and issue necessary instructions to the concerned Investigating Officer.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the instant criminal misc. petition is disposed of as not pressed with liberty to the petitioner to submit a detailed representation to the concerned Superintendent of Police averring therein all the grounds which have been raised in this petition within a period of 07 days from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.

3. In the event, the representation is submitted, the concerned Superintendent of Police is directed to minutely and objectively consider the contents of the same and thereafter, issue necessary instructions to the Investigating Officer.
All the relevant documents with the representation shall also be taken into consideration.
The representation shall be decided within a period of 30 days from the date of receipt of the same.
The parties will be at liberty to approach this Court again, if grievance arises.
4. Till 30 days from the date of filing of representation, the petitioner shall not be arrested in connection with FIR No.245/2025, registered at the Police Station Osian, District Jodhpur Rural.

sentences.text: 5. The offences alleged against the petitioner are under Sections 420, 406 and 120-B of the IPC.

Thus, the provisions contained under Section 35 of BNSS (Sections 41 and 41A of the CrPC) are applicable mutatis mutandis and the judgment rendered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar [AIR 2014 SC 2756] applies squarely in the present [2025:RJ-JD:35095] (3 of 3) [CRLMP-6354/2025] case, therefore, it is deemed appropriate to direct the investigating officer that in the event, the offences are found to be proved and the arrest of the petitioner is absolutely necessary, then instead of affecting arrest at once, a prior notice of 15 days shall be given to the petitioner.

Stay petition also stands disposed of.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Accordingly, the instant criminal misc. petition is disposed of as not pressed with liberty to the petitioner to submit a detailed representation to the concerned Superintendent of Police averring therein all the grounds which have been raised in this petition within a period of 07 days from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
3. In the event, the representation is submitted, the concerned Superintendent of Police is directed to minutely and objectively consider the contents of the same and thereafter, issue necessary instructions to the Investigating Officer.
All the relevant documents with the representation shall also be taken into consideration.
The representation shall be decided within a period of 30 days from the date of receipt of the same.
The parties will be at liberty to approach this Court again, if grievance arises.
4. Till 30 days from the date of filing of representation, the petitioner shall not be arrested in connection with FIR No.245/2025, registered at the Police Station Osian, District Jodhpur Rural.
5. The offences alleged against the petitioner are under Sections 420, 406 and 120-B of the IPC.
Further the petitioner shall also be at liberty to raise all permissible objections and issues before the trial court at the appropriate stage of proceedings 6.
Stay petition also stands disposed of.
